profile.name: Pratheek Eranki
profile.title: Software Engineer · AI & Data
profile.headline: Building software. Making data useful.
profile.intro: I work across software engineering and research data workflows, from enterprise applications to sleep EEG and fMRI research, and build full-stack, AI agent, and machine learning projects.

highlights.label: Co-authored, accepted in Computers in Biology and Medicine
Project case studies with linked evidence

profile.resumeSummary: Software engineer with experience in enterprise application delivery, sleep EEG and fMRI research data preparation, and legislative data analysis. Builds full-stack applications and AI/data projects using Python, Java, SQL, React, and machine learning tools. Co-author of the Rhamba research publication.

experience.summary: Contributed to software and data workflows supporting sleep EEG and fMRI research in a clinical research environment.
experience.imageAlt: Illustration of multichannel sleep EEG traces beside an fMRI voxel grid.
bullets: Prepared and validated sleep EEG and fMRI data for downstream research analysis, resolving data-quality and formatting issues while maintaining traceable processing steps.
Used PyTorch and TensorFlow in research workflows involving Transformers, self-attention, and Mamba architectures; supported model preparation, training, and fine-tuning experiments.
Worked with CBraMod-based EEG sleep-staging workflows and self-supervised fMRI experiments, connecting data preparation with model inputs and downstream evaluation.
Collaborated with researchers to translate study requirements into repeatable processing and analysis workflows, and developed utilities to reduce repetitive preparation work.
Documented processing procedures, validation checks, experiment configurations, and technical decisions so research workflows could be reproduced, reviewed, and maintained.

experience.summary: Conducted data-focused research using legislative records obtained through LegiScan.
experience.imageAlt: Illustration of legislative documents flowing into a standardized table and then into charts.
bullets: Built reproducible workflows to collect legislative records through the LegiScan API, clean source data, and organize structured SQL datasets for research analysis.
Standardized bill identifiers, jurisdictions, legislative status, sponsors, and subject classifications to support consistent comparisons across legislative records.
Used SQL and Excel to clean, deduplicate, and align legislative records with demographic data by state and year for comparative analysis.
Performed exploratory analysis of legislative activity and prepared Tableau and Plotly views to communicate trends and structured findings for faculty review.
Documented data definitions, transformation logic, API collection steps, and known limitations so research workflows and datasets could be reproduced and extended.

experience.summary: Contributed to enterprise software delivery in client-facing engineering environments.
experience.imageAlt: Illustration of a React form sending a REST request to a Spring Boot service backed by MySQL.
bullets: Developed and maintained Java Spring Boot application components and REST APIs within established development, testing, and release processes.
Built and maintained React and TypeScript interface components for data display, form validation, and application workflows, integrating them with backend services.

Worked with MySQL queries and indexing to support application data access and reporting; investigated software defects, documented root causes, and coordinated fixes with engineering and business stakeholders.
Supported JUnit testing, Docker-based environments, AWS deployment workflows, CI/CD, release validation, and production issue resolution across iterative software deliveries.
Participated in Agile delivery and code reviews, and created technical documentation and handoff materials explaining application behavior, recurring issues, and maintenance procedures.

projects.title: Rhamba
projects.summary: Region-aware self-supervised learning for resting-state fMRI, combining Attention and Mamba architectures.
projects.imageAlt: Schematic of the Rhamba workflow: fMRI, region-aware masking, hybrid encoder, downstream evaluation. This is an explanatory diagram, not measured brain data.
projects.problem: Learn useful representations from resting-state fMRI while studying how anatomical masking and sequence-model architecture affect downstream performance.
projects.contribution: Co-authored the Rhamba publication on region-aware self-supervised fMRI representation learning. The linked paper provides the study and full author list.
approach: Compared region-aware masking strategies and hybrid Attention-Mamba configurations.
Evaluated pretrained representations on downstream classification tasks.
Examined model behavior and interpretability across configurations.

evaluation.text: The paper reports downstream evaluation on COBRE and ADHD-200 after ABIDE pretraining. Results depend on both dataset and configuration; the paper provides the full experimental comparison.

limitations: Research results do not establish clinical diagnostic performance.
Configuration-dependent findings should be read alongside the paper's experimental setup.

publication.title: Rhamba: Region-Aware Hybrid Attention-Mamba Framework for Self-Supervised Learning in Resting-State fMRI
publication.authors: Pankaj Pandey, Ruthwik Reddy Doodipala, Pratheek Eranki, Carolina Torres-Rojas, Manob Jyoti Saikia, Ranganatha Sitaram
publication.status: Accepted for publication in Computers in Biology and Medicine, as reported by the arXiv record.

projects.title: FixBot
projects.summary: A conversational troubleshooting agent that connects symptom lookup, repair pricing, and semantic document search.
projects.role: Application implementation across agent orchestration, API, tools, and interface.
projects.imageAlt: FixBot application showing its chat interface, device selector, and example troubleshooting questions.
projects.problem: Turn a device problem into a grounded response with supporting symptom information, repair-cost estimates, and a clear next step.
projects.contribution: Implemented a custom iterative tool-calling loop, structured lookup tools, session memory, FastAPI endpoints, and a Gradio interface showing tool activity.
approach: Dispatches three tools for symptoms, pricing, and FAISS-backed knowledge search.
Feeds tool results back into an OpenAI-compatible NVIDIA NIM model until a response is ready.
Keeps a sliding window of conversation history and exposes the API separately from the interface.

evaluation.text: The repository includes unit tests for the lookup and pricing tools. The interface exposes calls and results for inspection; no measured end-to-end diagnosis accuracy is claimed here.

limitations: Repair costs and symptom matches come from curated example knowledge bases.
In-process conversation memory is intended for a project deployment; a shared persistent store would be needed for multiple workers.
A labeled end-to-end evaluation would be the next step before broader deployment.

projects.title: HomeSearch
projects.summary: A property search application with a Spring Boot API, PostgreSQL storage, and a React interface with map-based search.
projects.role: Full-stack application, ingestion, search API, and container configuration.
projects.imageAlt: HomeSearch screenshot with property filters, listing cards, and an interactive map.
projects.problem: Make a sizeable property dataset searchable through filters, pagination, and an interactive geographic interface.
projects.contribution: Implemented the Spring Boot service and React interface, including ingestion, listing details, city autocomplete, and map viewport search.
approach: Seeds generated listings into PostgreSQL and exposes paginated search endpoints.
Uses React, Leaflet, and Recharts for map exploration and listing details.
Packages the database, API, and frontend with Docker Compose; includes JUnit/MockMvc tests and a JMeter plan.

evaluation.text: The project seeds 51,000 generated listings. A JMeter load-test plan and backend tests are available in the repository; a reproducible latency comparison still needs hardware, workload, and percentile context.

limitations: The listing dataset is generated for demonstration.
A reproducible latency report needs the hardware, database state, workload, and percentile measurements.

projects.title: Academic RAG QA
projects.summary: Local academic question answering with FAISS retrieval, quantized Mistral inference, and four query routes.
projects.role: Course project implementation and baseline evaluation.
projects.problem: Compare document-grounded generation against the same local model answering without retrieved context.
projects.contribution: Built ingestion, retrieval, generation, query routing, upload/re-indexing, and evaluation workflows.
approach: Ingests PDF, TXT, and Markdown into a FAISS index.
Routes queries to document retrieval, direct math, web search, or fallback generation.
Evaluates RAG and base Mistral on a ten-question textbook QA set.

evaluation.text: Saved aggregate results on 10 textbook questions. Higher is better for these overlap metrics; these results are a small development benchmark.

limitations: Ten questions do not establish general performance or robustness.
Overlap metrics do not measure factual grounding or citation quality on their own.
Inference requires appropriate local hardware; the four routing paths need a broader evaluation.

projects.title: DriftBoard
projects.summary: A campaign analytics dashboard combining hypothesis tests, false-discovery correction, and KPI anomaly detection.
projects.role: Analytics pipeline, statistical testing, and dashboard implementation.
projects.imageAlt: DriftBoard experiment browser with an effect-size and significance plot.
projects.problem: Help explore experiment effects and identify unusual KPI changes without treating every nominally significant test as a reliable finding.
projects.contribution: Implemented statistical comparisons, Benjamini-Hochberg correction, KPI anomaly analysis, and the Streamlit reporting interface.
approach: Loads example data or an optional AWS Athena source.
Combines experiment summaries and an effect-size/significance visualization.
Shows IQR and Z-score anomalies alongside KPI time series.

evaluation.text: The repository includes test modules for statistical testing and drift detection. The default demonstration uses synthetic data; no measured business uplift is claimed.

limitations: Statistical significance should be interpreted with effect size and experiment assumptions.
KPI anomaly flags identify unusual observations, not necessarily a causal problem.
The hosted demonstration may need to wake from inactivity.

projects.title: Air Quality Patterns
projects.summary: Pollution and weather analysis across 200+ cities, with AQI classification and clustering of pollution regimes.
projects.role: Collaborative course project with Sai Teja Koppolu.
projects.problem: Explore how pollution measurements vary by city and time, and compare supervised AQI labeling with unsupervised structure.
projects.contribution: Contributed to the data collection, preprocessing, model comparison, and visualization workflow.
approach: Combines pollutant and weather measurements from April–November 2025.
Compares tree-based classifiers and examines K-Means clusters with low-dimensional visualizations.
Summarizes geographical and temporal pollution patterns.

evaluation.text: The project report records 99.9% AQI-category accuracy for tree models. AQI categories are derived from pollutant measurements, so this result should be interpreted as category reconstruction, not future air-quality forecasting.

limitations: The reported accuracy needs a split-aware assessment and checks for target-derived inputs.
A forecasting claim would require future targets, chronological evaluation, and appropriate baselines.
City and season coverage limit generalization.

projects.title: Bank Marketing Models
projects.summary: An R-based comparison of classifiers on the UCI Bank Marketing data, with explicit class-imbalance trade-offs.
projects.role: Statistical analysis, classifier comparison, and reporting.
projects.problem: Compare models for identifying term-deposit subscriptions while distinguishing ranking quality from positive-class recall.
projects.contribution: Prepared the data, compared tree, SVM, and neural classifiers, and produced the statistical report.
approach: Uses an 80/20 stratified train/test split.
Compares accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and AUC.
Reports the neural model's F1 alongside the random forest's AUC rather than selecting on accuracy alone.

evaluation.text: Values from the saved model comparison. The analysis includes call duration, which is only known after the call.

limitations: Call duration cannot be used for pre-call campaign targeting; that use case requires retraining without it.
Encoding is fitted before the split in the current analysis; a stricter evaluation should fit preprocessing on training data only.
Results are specific to this historical dataset and split.

projects.title: Stock Forecasting Comparison
projects.signal: GRU had the lowest saved RMSE
projects.summary: A comparison of GRU, LSTM, and Transformer models for next-day Walmart closing-price prediction.
projects.problem: Study the behavior of different sequence architectures on a historical next-day prediction task.
projects.contribution: Compared model predictions and training behavior using shared saved evaluation outputs.
approach: Uses historical Walmart price data and a 60-day lookback.
Compares MAE, RMSE, and R² across three architectures.
Keeps the observed model ranking visible, including the Transformer's weaker result.

evaluation.text: Values reproduced from the saved comparison, in the scale used by that experiment. GRU performed best among these three models in this run.

limitations: The saved table does not include a naive last-price baseline.
A stronger evaluation should document chronological splitting and walk-forward results.
A single stock and experiment do not establish general predictive performance.

projects.title: Movie Analytics & Rating Models
projects.summary: Movie-rating analysis with feature engineering, statistical classifiers, and genre and release-period visualizations.
projects.role: Data preparation, feature engineering, and exploratory model comparison.
projects.problem: Explore the relationship between movie metadata, rating categories, and release patterns.
projects.contribution: Prepared movie features, compared statistical classifiers, and produced exploratory visualizations.
approach: Derives genre and release-period features from movie metadata.
Compares LDA, QDA, naive Bayes, and KNN classification approaches.
Uses cross-validation and confusion matrices to inspect model behavior.
A companion repository explores TMDB data collection, rating prediction, and genre trends; it is linked separately from the classifier comparison.

evaluation.text: The repository contains the analysis workflow, cross-validation comparisons, and plots for exploring rating categories and model behavior.

limitations: Current popularity and vote statistics can be unavailable at release time; any prospective prediction task needs a clearly defined observation date.
Classification and exploration are separate from a validated personalized recommendation system.

projects.title: Charity-AID
projects.summary: A Spring Boot application for donor records, donation receipts, aid requests, and administrative workflows.
projects.problem: Connect donation and aid administration in an application with structured records and role-aware access.
projects.contribution: Implemented application workflows around donor management, receipts, authentication, and persistence.
approach: Uses Spring Security and JWT-based access control.
Supports administrator TOTP, PDF receipt generation, and notification integration.
Persists records through Spring Data JPA and MySQL, with unit and integration tests.

evaluation.text: The repository documents the implementation and its unit and integration tests. Application workflows can be inspected through the code and test scenarios.

limitations: Email and deployment integrations require separate configuration.
Production readiness requires operational review beyond the scope of a portfolio demonstration.

projects.title: OpsFlow
projects.summary: A team workflow application with organization-scoped projects, live Kanban boards, and incident tracking.
projects.role: Backend services, application workflows, and frontend integration.
projects.problem: Keep project work and incident updates in a shared application while separating organizations and supporting live collaboration.
projects.contribution: Implemented team and ticket workflows across Spring Boot services and the React interface, including role-aware access and real-time updates.
approach: Scopes organizations, users, projects, and tickets through authenticated APIs.
Uses WebSockets for board updates and Kafka for activity events.
Combines PostgreSQL persistence, Redis caching, and container-based development.

evaluation.text: The repository provides the application, deployment configuration, and a test entry point. The hosted demonstration offers a way to inspect the workflow; no load or uptime result is asserted.

limitations: Organization isolation and authorization require ongoing security testing before real team data is used.
Free-hosted services can take time to start after inactivity.

projects.title: FieldVerify
projects.summary: A provider site-visit prototype with mobile-ID integration, manual matching, and an auditable result history.
projects.role: Verification workflow, API integration, matching logic, and application interfaces.
projects.problem: Help a site-visit auditor distinguish a credential's authenticity from whether its attributes match an enrollment record.
projects.contribution: Built the workflow around separate authenticity and matching signals, manual fallback, SDK integration, and a chained audit log.
approach: Uses a FastAPI backend with React and Android interfaces.
Separates cryptographic credential checks from record-match scoring.
Records outcomes in a SHA-256-chained audit trail and includes tests for matching, audit behavior, and verification paths.

evaluation.text: The demonstration uses synthetic provider data. The repository explicitly labels its verified mobile-ID screenshot as using a stubbed Credence response; that image is not evidence of live end-to-end verification.

limitations: A manual record match is not cryptographic verification.
Live SDK behavior depends on the configured identity profile and available claims.
The Android device token is a prototype mechanism; a production deployment needs stronger device authentication.
projects.imageAlt: FieldVerify visit dashboard with synthetic provider records and visit statuses.

projects.title: DemandSense
projects.summary: A retail-demand forecasting project connecting feature generation, model experiments, an API, and drift reporting.
projects.role: Forecasting pipeline, experiment tracking, serving, and monitoring integration.
projects.problem: Connect retail forecasting experiments to an inspectable prediction service and monitoring workflow.
projects.contribution: Implemented the project workflow from feature preparation and model comparison through serving and dashboard integration.
approach: Builds lag, rolling, and calendar features from store-item sales histories.
Compares seasonal naive, gradient-boosted, and recurrent-model approaches with experiment tracking.
Exposes forecasts through FastAPI and a Streamlit dashboard, with drift reports and API/feature tests.

evaluation.text: The README describes expanding-window evaluation and WAPE comparisons. This case study links the full implementation without promoting README scores as independently reproduced results.

limitations: Time-series feature generation and splits must be checked together for leakage.
Model comparisons need a saved evaluation artifact, horizon, and baseline definition for reproducibility.
Historical store-item performance does not establish future inventory or revenue impact.

projects.title: Customer Operations Agent
projects.summary: A support-agent prototype combining tool use, escalation rules, prompt comparisons, and an inspection dashboard.
projects.role: Implemented a project prototype with mock account tools, prompt iteration, routing rules, and monitoring views.
projects.problem: Explore how an assistant can handle common account and transaction questions while handing sensitive cases to a human or risk queue.
projects.contribution: Implemented a project prototype with mock account tools, prompt iteration, routing rules, and monitoring views.
approach: Routes among six customer-support intent categories.
Uses four mock tools for account, transaction, risk, and human handoff workflows.
Separates offline synthetic-data evaluation from live model execution.

evaluation.text: The repository contains 1,250 generated test cases and separate offline/live evaluation modes. Simulated interaction logs are not evidence of deployed customer outcomes.

limitations: This is a personal prototype themed around a customer-operations use case, not a claim of employment or deployment at Hard Rock Digital.
Mock tools do not access real customer accounts.
Offline and live-model results must be reported separately.

projects.title: SegmentWise
projects.summary: A dashboard for exploring customer segments, churn models, campaign response, and model explanations.
projects.role: Built the segmentation, prediction, explanation, and dashboard workflow.
projects.problem: Connect customer-group exploration with model behavior and accessible analytical reporting.
projects.contribution: Built the segmentation, prediction, explanation, and dashboard workflow.
approach: Groups customer profiles using K-Means.
Models churn and campaign response with XGBoost.
Surfaces segment summaries, PCA views, and SHAP explanations in Streamlit.

evaluation.text: The repository includes the pipeline and model-inspection views. A targeting-lift claim requires a defined evaluation population, baseline, and saved experiment output.

limitations: Dashboard examples and offline model scores do not establish realized campaign uplift.
Segments depend on the input population and feature definitions.
projects.imageAlt: SegmentWise dashboard showing segment-level churn and response comparisons.

projects.title: Fraud Detection & Explanations
projects.summary: A transaction-classification experiment using XGBoost, imbalance handling, and global and local model explanations.
projects.role: Implemented feature preparation, model training, saved evaluation summaries, and SHAP visualizations.
projects.problem: Study precision/recall trade-offs and model explanations when positive examples are rare.
projects.contribution: Implemented feature preparation, model training, saved evaluation summaries, and SHAP visualizations.
approach: Generates 100,000 synthetic transactions with approximately 1% fraud labels.
Uses class weighting, log transforms, and cyclical time features.
Examines average precision and positive-class behavior alongside ROC-AUC.

evaluation.text: The saved synthetic-data summary reports average precision 0.9981 and fraud recall 0.9930. These scores describe the generated benchmark, not real financial transactions.

limitations: Synthetic labels may be much easier to predict than real fraud.
Deployment would need independent real-world validation and calibrated operating thresholds.

projects.title: E-Commerce Database Design
projects.summary: A MySQL database project for an e-commerce and multi-level distributor workflow, with generated data and analytical SQL.
projects.role: Contributed to a group database-systems project covering relational design, seed generation, and SQL analysis.
projects.problem: Model connected customer, order, product, and distributor records with consistent relationships and useful analytical queries.
projects.contribution: Contributed to a group database-systems project covering relational design, seed generation, and SQL analysis.
approach: Defines entities and relationships for orders, products, distributors, and commissions.
Generates synthetic records for query development.
Includes views, indexes, and EXPLAIN-plan investigation.

evaluation.text: The repository exposes the schema and SQL artifacts. No undocumented query-speed improvement or production transaction volume is claimed.

limitations: This is an academic group project using generated data.
Performance conclusions require a recorded workload and reproducible query plans.

projects.title: CBraMod on ISRUC
projects.summary: EEG representation-learning experiments adapting an existing CBraMod model to ISRUC sleep data.
projects.role: Adapted data preparation, pretraining and fine-tuning scripts, and patch visualizations around the existing CBraMod architecture.
projects.problem: Explore the preparation and training workflow for a pretrained EEG architecture on sleep-staging data.
projects.contribution: Adapted data preparation, pretraining and fine-tuning scripts, and patch visualizations around the existing CBraMod architecture.
approach: Prepares ISRUC EEG inputs for patch-based training.
Provides modified pretraining and downstream fine-tuning entry points.
Visualizes how EEG segments become model inputs.

evaluation.text: Training and evaluation entry points are available in the repository. A comparable held-out sleep-staging benchmark is not asserted without the split definition and saved results.

limitations: CBraMod is an existing architecture; this project is an adaptation and experiment workflow.
Subject-level separation and a documented evaluation protocol are necessary for interpretable results.
